chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Parents are liable for ingratitude/disobedience towards their children, if the child is righteous, to the same extent that the child is liable to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the reciprocal obligation between parents and righteous children in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to illustrate the concept of *'uquq* (disobedience/ingratitude) as a bidirectional moral bond, emphasizing that righteous children hold parents accountable for their upbringing. This reciprocal duty underscores that parental authority carries the weight of responsibility, where neglect or mistreatment of a virtuous child constitutes a spiritual liability for the parents.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-77 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“Parents might be damned by their children if they do not honor their rights just as children could be damned by their parents should they not honor their parents’ rights.”
